title: The public release id is not content-addressed: data_release_id = sig-<as-of date>-<sha256(as-of date, belief date, ruleset, resolver)[:8]> carries no spine content, watermark or commit, so different exports on the same UTC day share one id
evidence: Code: BuildSpec.content_key() = sha256(canonical_json({as_of_snapshot (date), as_of_belief (date), ruleset_version, resolver_version})); release_id() = f'{slug}-{as_of_snapshot}-{content_key[:8]}' (manifest.py:78-108); run_spine_export builds it from as_of[:10] (spine_export.py:2107-2114). Recompute (18:47:56Z, uv run python -c BuildSpec(...).release_id() with ruleset p27.3/1.0.0, resolver 0.0.0): 2026-09-24 -> sig-2026-09-24-bd01cb94, 2026-09-27 -> sig-2026-09-27-ce480ab1, 2026-09-28 -> sig-2026-09-28-30e3add6 = exactly the launch id (LAUNCH_RECORD_2026-09-24.md:27), the live id (REPUBLISH_LIVE_2026-09-27.md:18) and the 1-site composed-fixture id (p33.2-composed-verification/export/manifest.json). Live-read (18:46:24-36Z, gcloud storage ls -l / objects describe): the two 2026-09-24 national exports have manifest.json of identical size 34,631 B but different md5 (vkygLoO8wvdSdzFlijmrgQ== vs fvhR4VyZpcGIZEVrsv9HuA==) and bundle totals 924,457,431 vs 924,496,399 B. Inference (manifests not opened): both carry release_id sig-2026-09-24-bd01cb94 for different bytes. manifest.py:102 describes release_id as the Zenodo version DOI identity, so a same-day re-export deposit would collide; a fixture export and a production export on one day are indistinguishable by id. Docstring 'changes iff any reproducibility input changes' holds only because the inputs are date-granular. Design fix: G3 §3.1/§3.2 (export id over instants+watermark+commit; label sig-YYYY-MM-DD.N; p-<sha256> descriptor v2).

title: The live release was not belief-pinned (belief_pinned: false in its own artifacts; export.sh never passes --belief) yet records as_of_belief as the as-of date and every page calls its permalink 'Belief-pinned (reproducible after SIG corrects itself)'; the recorded belief cut cannot be reproduced even by a working resolver
evidence: export.sh builds 'python -m exports build --from-spine --dsn … --as-of "$SIG_EXPORT_AS_OF" --note … --out …' with no --belief (grep -c belief ops/gcp/export.sh -> 0 at 18:47:56Z). With belief=None the reads use upper_inf(c.sys_period) (current belief at snapshot time, shaping.py:1643-1646) while BuildSpec sets as_of_belief = as_of date (spine_export.py:2107-2108) and each web surface echoes as_of_belief = as_of[:10] with belief_pinned = False (spine_export.py:750-755). The C3 capture of the live public web/dossier_index.json (docs/build/logs/next-phase/C3/bucket/web/dossier_index.json sha256 a4938e6842e27cd6b82622353e34c7e568d34a15bf6c29f07a52b5b1635ab1ca) has 55 'belief_pinned': false and 0 true (count at 18:49:18Z); PROTOCOL.md:119 records the same. Citation.astro:60 renders 'Belief-pinned permalink (reproducible after SIG corrects itself)' on every page. The export ran 2026-09-27T00:51Z (REPUBLISH_LIVE §0), so a re-export 'as of belief 2026-09-27' would include claims asserted later that day: the data-layer cause is independent of F-07/C2 NEW-4 (nginx ignores the query string). Design fix: G3 §3.2 (belief instant = snapshot now(), belief_pinned true, watermark) and §5.3 (path-pinned snapshots).

title: Release code identity is unverifiable: resolver_version and renderer.version are the placeholder 0.0.0 in every release (09-24, 09-27 and the GATE-G3-signed p-17b713) because 11 of 14 packages hard-code __version__ = '0.0.0' while every pyproject says 0.1.0, and renderer.revision is unchecked free text
evidence: grep: __version__ = "0.0.0" in evidence, exports, ops, connectors, reconcile, db, inference, orchestration, parsing, tasks, resolution (11); 0.1.0 in api, ontology, policy; all 14 pyproject.toml 'version = "0.1.0"'; web/package.json 0.1.0. run_spine_export: resolver_version = resolver_version or exports.__version__ (spine_export.py:2113), so the manifest records the exporter's placeholder, not a resolver identity: the live public manifest.json carries resolver 0.0.0 (J1 research/J1-exposure-inventory.md:107), and the NEW-1 recompute reproduces the 09-24 and 09-27 ids only with resolver_version 0.0.0 and the signed candidate descriptor has resolver_version 0.0.0 and renderer {package sig-exports, version 0.0.0, revision a33cd6ec…}. 'sig-exports release build --renderer-revision' is a required free-text flag documented as 'never auto-detected' (cli.py:272-276) and nothing checks it names a commit or the checked-out tree; composed_verify passes the default 'p33.2' (composed_verify.py:256). SIG-FIND-001 requires the release manifest to pin code; SIG-EXPORT-003 names the resolver version as a reproducibility input. C2 NEW-28 (methodology omits resolver version) is the display symptom only. Design fix: G3 §3.2, §9.3 (one version source; commit from a clean pushed tree).

title: The withdrawal deny include is read only when nginx starts and no reload or roll path exists: a withdrawal written to the gcsfuse-mounted bucket leaves aliases served 200 by running instances while newly started instances deny them (latent until the P32.13 nginx is deployed)
evidence: nginx.conf:143 'include /mnt/sig-web/conf/withdrawn_*.conf;' with the comment 'The file is generated by sig-ops release-serve apply on every staging run'; release_serving.apply and exports.release.record_withdrawal only write files (tombstones + conf) and never signal nginx; grep for 'nginx -s reload' across ops/ and exports/src -> 0 (18:49:18Z). Inference (standard nginx semantics): include files are read at start/reload only, so on Cloud Run (sig-web min 0, autoscaled) instances started before a withdrawal keep serving the alias routes (index.html, .json, entity stubs — the ED-16 aliases the exact-match map is meant to deny) while instances started after deny them; canonical routes are tombstoned in bytes immediately, aliases are not. Latent: the live sig-web image 5c064881 has no include at all (G2 §1, G2 NEW-2). G2 ACT-17 noted 'a documented way to make a new withdrawal take effect (inference)' as scope; this finding adds the per-instance divergence and the absence of any mechanism. Design fix: G3 §4.2/§8.3 (immutable conf generations selected per revision + roll on withdraw; conf-gen regression probe).

title: Release trees and staging registries are committed to the public repository (898 /r/p-… files and 84 registry files under docs/build/reports/); the P32.25 'staging' registry is therefore public, and a real candidate staged the same way would be published before sign-off
evidence: git ls-files 'docs/build/reports/*' | grep -c '/r/p-' -> 898; git ls-files 'docs/build/reports/*/staging_registry/*' 'docs/build/reports/*/registry/*' | wc -l -> 84 (18:49:18Z); p32.25 staging_registry holds catalog.json, latest.json, compat_index.json, activations/, staged/ (49 files) — F-15 notes it is committed. gh repo view (18:35:42Z) -> visibility PUBLIC (E1 NEW-14). The committed trees are fixture/synthetic (F-15: 0 records, example.test evidence), so no harm today; the hazard is the pattern: G2 step 3 assumes a staged candidate is 'none public', which holds only if candidate trees and registries never enter the repo (national scale ~475k files / 2.0 GB would also be unreviewable). Design rule: G3 RM-8 (the repo records digests, labels and readouts only; candidates live in the private release bucket).

title: J3's /s/<pub>/ page-snapshot build assumes base-path support the web code lacks: no base in astro.config.mjs, 0 BASE_URL uses and 85 root-absolute path sites in 36 files, so snapshot pages would link out of the pinned copy without an unsized refactor
evidence: astro.config.mjs defines site and trailingSlash but no base; grep -rn 'BASE_URL\|base:' web/src web/astro.config.mjs -> 0; grep -rcE 'href="/|`/[a-z]' web/src -> 85 occurrences in 36 files (18:47:42Z) — literal hrefs plus template-literal paths in lib/ and islands (e.g. tile/style fetch paths). J3 §8.1 designs 'the same export-mode Astro build runs twice — base / and base /s/<pub>/' and J3 TX-13b is sized L without this refactor. Root-absolute links ignore <base href>, so a snapshot page's links would resolve into the mutable latest view, defeating page-level pinning (J3 NEW-1). Design: G3 §5.3 containment rule (SIG-REL-D08) and the J3 §8.1 fallback until a withBase() refactor lands in TX-13b.
